﴿And persisted﴾, i.e., they continued in disbelief, did not desist from it, and did not repent of it. ﴿And grew arrogant﴾ from accepting the truth and from carrying out what he commanded them, ﴿with great arrogance﴾.

﴿Then indeed I called them openly﴾, i.e., I made the call manifest to them, proclaiming it to them.

﴿Then indeed I announced to them﴾, i.e., I called them, declaring openly to them through the call, ﴿and I spoke to them in private, in secret﴾, i.e., I made the call to them privately, in much secrecy. It was said: the meaning is that he would call one man after another, speaking to him secretly between himself and him. The intent is that he called them in various ways and different methods, but that did not take effect among them.

Mujahid said: the meaning of "I announced" is "I shouted." It was also said: the meaning of "I spoke in secret" is: I came to them in their homes and called them there.

The accusative of "openly" (jiharan) is as a verbal noun (masdar), because calling can be done openly and can be done not openly. So "openly" is a kind of calling, like the saying: "He sat the qurfusaʾ" (a squatting posture). It is also permissible that it be an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e., "a calling openly," and that it be a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial (hal), i.e., "openly proclaiming." The meaning of "then" (thumma) is to indicate the distance between the states, because openness is more severe than secrecy, and combining the two is more severe than either one.

Ibn ʿAmir... [the reading] — The majority read "innī" with sukun on the ya; Abu ʿAmr and the Makkans and Madinans read it with fatha.

﴿So I said: "Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving"﴾, i.e., ask Him for forgiveness of your past sins with sincere intention. ﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving﴾, i.e., He is abundantly forgiving to the sinners. It was also said: the meaning of "ask forgiveness" is "repent of disbelief; indeed He is ever Forgiving to those who repent."

﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾, i.e., He will send the rain of the sky upon you, so there is an implied element. It was also said: what is meant by "the sky" is rain, as in the saying of the poet:

When the sky descends upon the land of a people, we graze upon it, even if they are angry.

"Midrar" means abundant pouring, i.e., flowing with rain. Its accusative is either as a circumstantial of "the sky" — and it is not feminized because mif'al does not take the feminine form; one says: "a woman who bears only females (mi'nath) and a male-bearing one (midhkar)" — or it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e., "a sending abundant." The discussion of this has already occurred in Surat al-Anʿam. "Yursil" is in the jussive because it is the answer to the command.

In this verse is evidence that asking forgiveness is among the greatest causes of rain and the attainment of all kinds of provision. For this reason He said: ﴿and will aid you with wealth and sons, and will make for you gardens﴾, meaning orchards, ﴿and will make for you rivers﴾, flowing.

ʿAta' said: the meaning is: He will increase your wealth and your children.

Noah, peace be upon him, informed them that their faith in Allah gathers for them, together with abundant share in the Hereafter, fertility and wealth in this world.

﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect for Allah any dignity?﴾, i.e., what excuse do you have for abandoning hope? Here "hope" means fear: i.e., "What is the matter with you that you do not fear Allah?" "Waqar" means greatness, from tawqir, which is venerating. The meaning: you do not fear the true extent of His greatness, so that you would affirm His oneness and obey Him. The phrase ﴿lā tarjūna﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial of the addressees' pronoun, and the operative element in it is the sense of settledness in "lakum." Among the uses of "hope" for "fear" is the verse of the Hudhali:

When the bee stings him, he does not hope for its sting.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-ʿAliyah, and ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah said: "What is the matter with you that you do not expect from Allah a reward, nor do you fear from Him a punishment."

Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: "What is the matter with you that you do not care for Allah's greatness."

Qutrub said: this is a Hijazi dialect. Hudhayl, Khuzaʿah, and Mudar say: "lam arju" means "lam ubal" (I did not care).

Qatadah said: "What is the matter with you that you do not expect for Allah the outcome of faith."

Ibn Kaysan said: "What is the matter with you that you do not hope, in worshipping Allah and obeying Him, that He will reward you with good for your veneration of Him."

Ibn Zayd said: "What is the matter with you that you do not render to Allah obedience."

al-Hasan said: "What is the matter with you that you do not recognize for Allah a right, nor do you thank Him for a blessing."

The clause ﴿while He has created you in stages﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial, i.e., while the state is that He, glorified is He, has created you in various stages: a drop, then a clot, then a lump, until the completion of creation, as has already been explained in Surat al-Muʾminun. "Tawr" in the language means a time or occasion. Ibn al-Anbari said: "al-tawr" means state, and its plural is "aṭwar." It was also said: "aṭwar" means: children, then youths, then elders. It was also said: "al-aṭwar" are their differences in actions, sayings, and characters. The meaning: how do you fall short in venerating the One who created you in these wondrous stages?

﴿Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers?﴾ The address is to whoever is fit for it, and the intent is to argue from the creation of the heavens for His perfect power and wondrous craftsmanship, and that He is worthy of worship. "Tibaq" means those layered one above another, each heaven covering the other like domes.

al-Hasan said: Allah created seven heavens over seven earths; between each heaven and heaven, and earth and earth, there is creation and command. The verification of this has already been mentioned in His saying: ﴿and of the earth the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq: 12]. "Tibaqan" is in the accusative as a verbal noun: one says "tabaqahu mutabaqah and tibaqan"; or it is a circumstantial in the sense of "possessing layers," where "dhat" was omitted and "tibaqan" was placed in its position. al-Farraʾ permitted, outside the Qur'an, that "tibaqan" be in the genitive as an adjective.

﴿And made the moon therein a light﴾, i.e., illuminating the face of the earth. He made the moon within the heavens although it is in the lowest heaven, because when it is in one of them, it is in them all. So said Ibn Kaysan.

al-Akhfash said: just as you say, "The Banu Tamim came to me," and the intent is some of them.

Qutrub said: "fihinna" means "maʿahunna" (with them), i.e., He created the moon and the sun together with the creation of the heavens and the earth, as in the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

And will he enjoy who has the last of his covenant thirty months in three states?

i.e., with three states.

﴿And made the sun a lamp﴾, i.e., like a lamp for the people of the earth, so that they may thereby reach the management of what they need of livelihood.

﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a growth﴾ (p-1535) — meaning Adam, whom Allah created from the surface of the earth. The meaning: He brought you into being from it by creation. "Inbat" is used in place of "inshaʾ" because it is more indicative of origination and formation. "Nabatan" is either a verbal noun of "anbata" with the augmentations dropped, or a verbal noun of an omitted verb, i.e., "He made you grow from the earth, so you grew a growth."

al-Khalil and al-Zajjaj said: it is a verbal noun of an omitted verb: "He made you grow from the earth, so you grew a growth." And al-Khalil and al-Zajjaj said: it is a verbal noun carried over the sense, since the meaning of "He made you grow" is "He made you sprout a sprouting."

It was also said: the meaning is: Allah caused the plants to grow for you from the earth, so "nabatan" in this view is an object.

Ibn Bahr said: He made them grow in the earth, becoming great after being small, and tall after being short.

﴿Then He will return you into it﴾, i.e., into the earth, ﴿and will bring you out, a bringing out﴾, meaning He will bring you out from it by resurrection on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And Allah has made for you the earth a spread-out expanse﴾, i.e., He spread it out and laid it flat for you, so that you turn upon it as you turn upon your rugs in your houses.

﴿So that you may traverse therein roads, wide passages﴾, i.e., broad paths. "Fijaj" is the plural of "fajj," which is the wide road. So said al-Farraʾ and others. It was also said: the "fajj" is the way between two mountains. The verification of this has already passed in Surat al-Anbiya' and fully in Surat al-Hajj.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿they put their fingers in their ears﴾: he said, "So that they would not hear what he says." ﴿And covered themselves with their garments﴾: he said, "So that they would disguise themselves and he would not recognize them." ﴿And grew arrogant with great arrogance﴾: he said, "They abandoned repentance."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him: ﴿and covered themselves with their garments﴾: he said, "They covered their faces so that they would not see Noah nor hear his speech."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman narrated from him also, regarding His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect for Allah any dignity?﴾: he said, "You do not know for Allah any greatness."

Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him also: "Waqaran": he said, "greatness."

In his commentary on His words, ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾, he said: "(He created you first as) a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh."

Ibn Abi Hatim also related from him, as well: "You do not fear His punishment, nor do you hope for His reward."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, in his al-Musannaf, related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw some people bathing naked, without loincloths on them. He stopped and called out at the top of his voice: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not look for any majesty from God?﴾

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzamah related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "The sun and the moon have their faces toward the heaven and their backs toward the earth. I recite this to you, (confirming) that it is from the Book of God: ﴿and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp﴾."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzamah related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, who said: "(The moon) gives light to the inhabitants of the heavens just as it gives light to the inhabitants of the earth."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs and Kaʿb al-Ahbar met, and there had been some resentment between them, so they reproached one another, and that (resentment) went away. Then ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr said to Kaʿb: "Ask me whatever you wish. You will not ask me about anything except that I will inform you, by confirming my words from the Qur'an." So (Kaʿb) said to him: "Tell me, is the light of the sun and the moon in the seven heavens just as it is on the earth?" He said: "Yes. Have you not seen God's saying: ﴿God created seven heavens in layers and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp﴾?"

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzamah, and al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾, that he said: "Its face is in the heaven toward the Throne, and its back is toward the earth."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related through the chain of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from him (Ibn ʿAbbas) regarding ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾, that he said: "When He created them, He placed in them a radiance for the inhabitants of the earth, and there is none of its light in the heaven."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him as well regarding ﴿roads, wide paths﴾, that he said: "Different ways."

It was narrated by Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "The surah ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah﴾ was revealed at Mecca."

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people﴾. It has already been mentioned that Noah was the first messenger whom Allah sent, and he is Noah son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Enoch (Akhnukh), son of Kenan, son of Shith (Seth), son of Adam. The duration of his stay among his people and the full statement of his lifespan have already been mentioned, as has the age at which he was sent, in Surat al-ʿAnkabut. ﴿That warn your people﴾, i.e., "warn," with "an" being a verbal particle (masdariyyah). It is also possible that it is the explanatory "an" (mufassirah), since sending carries the meaning of saying.

Ibn Masʿud read "andhir" without "an," and this is on the basis of an implied "say" (al-qawl), i.e., "We said to him: warn," ﴿before there comes to them a painful punishment﴾, i.e., a punishment of severe pain, which is the punishment of the Fire.

al-Kalbi said: it is what came upon them of the flood.

The clause ﴿He said: "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner"﴾ is a resumptive clause (mustaʾnafah), an explanatory resumption (istiʾnaf bayani) on the assumption of a question, as if it were said: "What did Noah say?" So he said: he said to them, etc.

The meaning: I am to you a warner from the punishment of Allah, one who instills fear in you, and one who makes clear to you what your salvation lies in.

﴿That worship Allah, and fear Him, and obey me﴾. The "an" is explanatory for "nadhir," or it is the masdariyyah, i.e., "that you worship Allah and do not associate with Him anything else, and fear Him, i.e., avoid what would bring you into His punishment, and obey me in what I command you, for I am a messenger to you from Allah."

﴿He will forgive you of your sins﴾. This is the answer to the command, and "min" (of) is partitive, i.e., some of your sins, namely what has passed of them before obeying the Messenger and answering his call.

al-Suddi said: the meaning is "He will forgive you your sins," so "min" in this case is superfluous (zaʾidah). It was also said: the intended "some" is what does not relate to the rights of people. It was also said: it is for specifying the kind. It was also said: "He will forgive you of your sins" means what you have asked forgiveness for of them.

﴿And delay you until a specified term﴾, i.e., He will delay your death until the furthest limit which Allah has decreed for you, on condition of faith and obedience, beyond what He has decreed for you if you remain in disbelief and disobedience. It was also said: the delay means blessing in their lifespans if they believe, and the absence of blessing in them if they do not believe.

Muqatil said: "He will delay you until the end of your appointed terms."

al-Zajjaj said: i.e., He will delay you from the punishment, so that you die not in the manner of those who are uprooted by punishment.

al-Farraʾ said: the meaning is that He will not make you die by drowning, burning, or killing. ﴿Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not deferred﴾, i.e., what He has decreed for you, on the assumption that you remain in disbelief, of punishment, when it comes while you remain in disbelief, is not deferred but occurs without doubt. So hasten to faith and obedience.

It was also said: the meaning is: indeed the term of Allah, which is death, when it comes, faith is no longer possible for you. It was also said: the meaning is: when death comes it is not deferred, whether it is by punishment or not by punishment.

﴿If only you knew﴾, i.e., if you had any knowledge at all, you would have hastened to what I have commanded you, or you would have known that the term of Allah, when it comes, is not deferred.

﴿He said: "My Lord, indeed I have called my people night and day"﴾. That is, Noah said, calling upon his Lord and relating to Him what took place between him and his people, though He is more knowing of it than he: "Indeed I have called my people to what You commanded me to call them to, of faith, calling continuously by night and by day, without any shortcoming."

(p-1534) ﴿But my calling only increased them in flight﴾ from what I called them to, and distance from it.

Muqatil said: "That is, distance from faith." Attributing the increase to the calling is because it was its cause, as in His saying: ﴿it increased them in faith﴾ [al-Anfal: 2].

﴿And indeed, whenever I called them, that You might forgive them﴾, i.e., whenever I called them to the cause of forgiveness, which is faith in You and obedience to You, ﴿they put their fingers in their ears﴾ so that they would not hear my voice, ﴿and covered themselves with their garments﴾, i.e., they covered their faces with them so that they would not see me. It was also said: they placed their garments over their heads so that they would not hear my words; the covering with garments on this view is an added measure of stopping the ears. It was also said: it is a metaphor for enmity; it is said: "So-and-so put on the garments of enmity." It was also said: they covered their garments so that he would not recognize them and call them.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman narrated from him also, regarding His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect for Allah any dignity?﴾: he said, "You do not know for Allah any greatness."

Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him also: "Waqaran": he said, "greatness."

In his commentary on His words, ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾, he said: "(He created you first as) a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh."

Ibn Abi Hatim also related from him, as well: "You do not fear His punishment, nor do you hope for His reward."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, in his al-Musannaf, related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw some people bathing naked, without loincloths on them. He stopped and called out at the top of his voice: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not look for any majesty from God?﴾

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzamah related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "The sun and the moon have their faces toward the heaven and their backs toward the earth. I recite this to you, (confirming) that it is from the Book of God: ﴿and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp﴾."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzamah related from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, who said: "(The moon) gives light to the inhabitants of the heavens just as it gives light to the inhabitants of the earth."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs and Kaʿb al-Ahbar met, and there had been some resentment between them, so they reproached one another, and that (resentment) went away. Then ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr said to Kaʿb: "Ask me whatever you wish. You will not ask me about anything except that I will inform you, by confirming my words from the Qur'an." So (Kaʿb) said to him: "Tell me, is the light of the sun and the moon in the seven heavens just as it is on the earth?" He said: "Yes. Have you not seen God's saying: ﴿God created seven heavens in layers and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp﴾?"

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzamah, and al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾, that he said: "Its face is in the heaven toward the Throne, and its back is toward the earth."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related through the chain of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from him (Ibn ʿAbbas) regarding ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾, that he said: "When He created them, He placed in them a radiance for the inhabitants of the earth, and there is none of its light in the heaven."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him as well regarding ﴿roads, wide paths﴾, that he said: "Different ways."

**Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, on Surah 71, verses 21–28**

His saying: ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me"﴾, meaning they persisted in their disobedience and did not respond to my call. He complained of them to God, Mighty and Majestic, and informed Him that they had disobeyed him and had not followed him, though He knows this best. ﴿And they followed one whose wealth and children increased him only in loss﴾, meaning the lowly followed their leaders and the wealthy among them, whose abundance of wealth and children increased them only in misguidance in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

The people of Medina, the people of Syria, and ʿAsim, along with Waladuhu, read *wa-waladuhu* with a fatha on the *waw* and the *lam*.

The rest read it with a sukun on the *lam*. This is a dialectal form for "child" (*walad*). It may also be a plural. Its verification has already been discussed. The meaning of *wa-ittaba'u* ("and they followed") is that they persisted in following, not that they initiated the following.

﴿And they schemed a great scheme﴾, meaning a great, mighty scheme. It is said *kabīr*, *kubār*, and *kubbār*, like *ʿajīb*, *ʿujāb*, and *ʿujjāb*, and *jamīl*, *jumāl*, and *jummāl*.

Al-Mubarrad said: *kubbāran* with the doubled consonant is intensive, like *qurrāʾ* (very much reciting) for one who recites much. Ibn al-Sikkit recited:

*A fair one who hunts hearts and takes captive,*
*by beauty, the heart of the Muslim reciters.*

The majority read *kubbāran* with the doubled consonant. Ibn Muhaysin, Humayd, and Mujahid read it without doubling.

Abu Bakr said: it is the plural of *kabīr*, as though he made *makr* ("scheme") stand in place of *dhunūb* or *afāʿīl*, which is why he described it with the plural.

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: it is a Yemeni dialect form.

They differed about what this scheme was. It was said: it was their inciting their lowly ones to kill Noah. It was said: it was their deceiving people by means of the wealth and children they had been given, to the point that the weak said, "If they were not upon the truth, they would not have been given these blessings." (p-1536)

Al-Kalbi said: it was what they attributed to God of companions and offspring.

Muqatil said: it was the saying of their great ones to their followers, "Do not leave your gods." It was also said: their scheme was their disbelief.

﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods"﴾, meaning do not abandon the worship of your gods, which are the idols and images that they had. Later the Arabs worshipped them after them. This is the view of the majority. ﴿Nor Wadd, nor Suwāʿ, nor Yaghūth, nor Yaʿūq, nor Nasr﴾, meaning: do not abandon the worship of these.

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: these were names of righteous people who lived between Adam and Noah. After them, a generation arose that imitated them in worship. Iblis said to them, "If you made their images, it would be more invigorating for you and more conducive to worship." They did so. Then another generation arose after them, and Iblis said to them, "Those who came before you worshipped them, so worship them." The beginning of idol worship was from that time, and these images were named after these names because they had made them in the form of those people.

ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr and others said: these were names of Adam's children, and Wadd was the eldest of them.

Al-Mawardi said: as for Wadd, he was the first idol worshipped. He was named Wadd because of their love (*wudd*) for him. He was after the people of Noah, belonging to the tribe of Kalb at Dawmat al-Jandal, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtaʾ, and Muqatil. Their poet said of him:

*May Wadd greet you, for we are not permitted*
*the play of women, and religion has departed.*

As for Suwāʿ, it belonged to Hudhayl on the seacoast.

As for Yaghūth, it belonged to Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jurf in Saba, according to Qatadah.

Al-Mahdawi said: it belonged to Murad, then to Ghatafan. As for Yaʿūq, it belonged to Hamdan, according to Qatadah, Ikrimah, and ʿAtaʾ.

Al-Thaʿlabi said: it belonged to Kahlan ibn Saba, then they inherited it until it came to Hamdan. Malik ibn Namat al-Hamdani said of it:

*God makes feathers grow in this world and makes it fall away,*
*but Yaʿūq does not make it fall away, nor does he make feathers grow.*

As for Nasr, it belonged to Dhu al-Kalaʿ of Himyar, according to Qatadah and Muqatil.

The majority read *Waddan* with a fatha on the *waw*. Nafiʿ read it with a damma.

Al-Layth said: *Wudd* with a damma is an idol of Quraysh, and with a fatha it is an idol that belonged to the people of Noah. Amr ibn Wadd was named after it.

In *al-Sihah* it is said: *al-Wadd* with a fatha is a peg in the dialect of the people of Najd, as though they had made the *tāʾ* quiescent and assimilated it into the *dāl*.

The majority read *wa-lā Yaghūtha wa-Yaʿūqa* without tanwin. If they are Arabic, the prohibition from declension is due to proper-noun status and the form of the verb. If they are foreign, it is due to foreignness and proper-noun status.

Al-Aʿmash read *wa-lā Yaghūthan wa-Yaʿūqan* with tanwin.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: that is an error.

The reason these idols are specifically mentioned, although they are included among the gods, is that they were the greatest and most important of their idols.

﴿And they have led many astray﴾, meaning their great ones and leaders led many people astray. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the idols, meaning that many people were led astray through them, like Abraham's saying: ﴿My Lord, they have led many people astray﴾ [Ibrahim: 36]. The pronoun for rational beings was applied to them because the disbelievers who worship them believe that they reason. ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in misguidance﴾ is coordinated with ﴿My Lord, they have disobeyed me﴾. The explicit noun was placed in place of the pronoun to record their wrongdoing against them.

Abu Hayyan said: it is coordinated with *qad aḍallū* ("they have led astray"). The meaning of ﴿except in misguidance﴾ is "except in punishment." Thus said Ibn Bahr, and he cited as evidence His saying: ﴿Indeed the criminals are in misguidance and madness﴾ [al-Qamar: 47]. It was also said: except in loss. It was also said: except in trial through wealth and children. It was also said: perdition. It was also said: misguidance in their scheme.

﴿Because of their sins they were drowned﴾. *Mā* is extra for emphasis, and the meaning is "because of their sins," that is, on account of them and because of them, they were drowned by the flood. ﴿Then they were made to enter a fire﴾ immediately after that, which is the fire of the Hereafter. It was also said: it is the punishment of the grave.

The majority read *khaṭīʾātihim* in the sound plural. Abu ʿAmr read *khaṭāyāhum* in the broken plural. Al-Jahdari, Amr ibn ʿUbayd, al-Aʿmash, Abu Hayawa, and Ashhab al-ʿUqayli read *khaṭīʾatihim* in the singular.

Al-Dahhak said: they were punished with fire in this world together with drowning, in one state: they were drowned on one side and burned on another.

The majority read *ughriqū* from *aghraqa*. Zayd ibn ʿAli read *ghurriqū* with doubling.

﴿Then they found for themselves no helpers besides God﴾, meaning they found no one to prevent them from God's punishment or to repel it from them.

﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as an inhabitant"﴾. This is coordinated with ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me"﴾. When Noah, peace be upon him, despaired of their faith and their turning away from disbelief, he invoked destruction against them.

Qatadah said: he invoked against them after it had been revealed to him: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]. God answered his supplication and drowned them.

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Muqatil, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, Ibn Zayd, and ʿAtiyyah said: he said this when God had brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women, and had made the wombs of women and the loins of men barren seventy years before the punishment. It was also said: forty years.

Qatadah said: there was no child among them at the time of the punishment.

Al-Hasan and Abu al-ʿAliyah said: if God had destroyed their children together with them, it would have been a punishment from God upon them and justice concerning them. But God destroyed their offspring and children without punishment, then destroyed them with punishment.

The meaning of *dayyāran* is one who inhabits dwellings. Its origin is *daywār*, on the pattern *fayʿāl*, from *dāra yadūru*. The *waw* was changed to a *yāʾ* and one of the two was assimilated into the other, like *al-qayyām*, whose origin is *qaywām*. Al-Qutaybi said: its origin is from *al-dār* ("the house"), meaning one who dwells in the house. It is said: *mā bi-l-dār dayyār*, meaning, "there is no one in the house." It was also said: *al-dayyār* is the owner of dwellings. The meaning is: do not spare anyone of them, but destroy him.

﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾, meaning if You leave them upon the earth, they will lead Your servants astray from the path of truth. ﴿And they will not beget except a wicked disbeliever﴾, meaning except one who will be wicked by abandoning Your obedience, a disbeliever of Your blessing, that is, one who greatly denies it. The meaning is: except one who will be wicked and will disbelieve.

Then, when he had invoked against the disbelievers, he followed it with supplication for himself, his parents, and the believers, saying: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾. They were both believers. His father was Lamak ibn Mutushalakh, as mentioned earlier, and his mother was Samhaʾ bint Anush. It was also said that he meant Adam and Eve.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: by "his parents" he meant his father and his grandfather.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr read *wa-li-wālidī* with a kasra on the *dāl*, in the singular.

﴿And for whoever enters my house﴾. Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: it means his mosque. It was also said: his dwelling in which he lived. It was also said: his ship. It was also said: whoever enters his religion. The accusative of *muʾminan* is circumstantial, meaning: whoever enters my house being characterized by the attribute of faith. Thus whoever enters it without being characterized by this attribute is excluded, such as his wife and his son, who said: ﴿I will take refuge in a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾ [Hud: 43]. Then he generalized the supplication, saying: ﴿and for the believing men and believing women﴾, meaning: forgive every person characterized by faith, male and female.

Then he returned to invoking against the disbelievers, saying: ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction﴾, meaning do not increase those characterized by wrongdoing except in ruin, loss, and destruction. His supplication included every wrongdoer until the Day of Resurrection, just as it included every believing man and believing woman until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Nor Wadd, nor Suwāʿ, nor Yaghūth, nor Yaʿūq, nor Nasr﴾, that he said: these idols were worshipped in the time of Noah.

Al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh related from him that he said: the idols that were worshipped among the people of Noah passed into the Arabs.

As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb at Dawmat al-Jandal. As for Suwāʿ, it belonged to Hudhayl. As for Yaghūth, it belonged to Murad, then to the Banu Ghutayf. As for Yaʿūq, it belonged to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Himyar, to the family of Dhu al-Kalaʿ. These were names of righteous men from the people of Noah. When they died, Satan revealed to their people: "Set up at their assembly place, where they used to sit, memorials (*anṣāb*), and name them after their names." They did so. It was not worshipped until those people had died, and knowledge was abrogated, and then it was worshipped.

**Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, on Surah 71, verses 21–28**

His saying: ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me"﴾, meaning they persisted in their disobedience and did not respond to my call. He complained of them to God, Mighty and Majestic, and informed Him that they had disobeyed him and had not followed him, though He knows this best. ﴿And they followed one whose wealth and children increased him only in loss﴾, meaning the lowly followed their leaders and the wealthy among them, whose abundance of wealth and children increased them only in misguidance in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

The people of Medina, the people of Syria, and ʿAsim, along with Waladuhu, read *wa-waladuhu* with a fatha on the *waw* and the *lam*.

The rest read it with a sukun on the *lam*. This is a dialectal form for "child" (*walad*). It may also be a plural. Its verification has already been discussed. The meaning of *wa-ittaba'u* ("and they followed") is that they persisted in following, not that they initiated the following.

﴿And they schemed a great scheme﴾, meaning a great, mighty scheme. It is said *kabīr*, *kubār*, and *kubbār*, like *ʿajīb*, *ʿujāb*, and *ʿujjāb*, and *jamīl*, *jumāl*, and *jummāl*.

Al-Mubarrad said: *kubbāran* with the doubled consonant is intensive, like *qurrāʾ* (very much reciting) for one who recites much. Ibn al-Sikkit recited:

*A fair one who hunts hearts and takes captive,*
*by beauty, the heart of the Muslim reciters.*

The majority read *kubbāran* with the doubled consonant. Ibn Muhaysin, Humayd, and Mujahid read it without doubling.

Abu Bakr said: it is the plural of *kabīr*, as though he made *makr* ("scheme") stand in place of *dhunūb* or *afāʿīl*, which is why he described it with the plural.

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: it is a Yemeni dialect form.

They differed about what this scheme was. It was said: it was their inciting their lowly ones to kill Noah. It was said: it was their deceiving people by means of the wealth and children they had been given, to the point that the weak said, "If they were not upon the truth, they would not have been given these blessings." (p-1536)

Al-Kalbi said: it was what they attributed to God of companions and offspring.

Muqatil said: it was the saying of their great ones to their followers, "Do not leave your gods." It was also said: their scheme was their disbelief.

﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods"﴾, meaning do not abandon the worship of your gods, which are the idols and images that they had. Later the Arabs worshipped them after them. This is the view of the majority. ﴿Nor Wadd, nor Suwāʿ, nor Yaghūth, nor Yaʿūq, nor Nasr﴾, meaning: do not abandon the worship of these.

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: these were names of righteous people who lived between Adam and Noah. After them, a generation arose that imitated them in worship. Iblis said to them, "If you made their images, it would be more invigorating for you and more conducive to worship." They did so. Then another generation arose after them, and Iblis said to them, "Those who came before you worshipped them, so worship them." The beginning of idol worship was from that time, and these images were named after these names because they had made them in the form of those people.

ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr and others said: these were names of Adam's children, and Wadd was the eldest of them.

Al-Mawardi said: as for Wadd, he was the first idol worshipped. He was named Wadd because of their love (*wudd*) for him. He was after the people of Noah, belonging to the tribe of Kalb at Dawmat al-Jandal, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtaʾ, and Muqatil. Their poet said of him:

*May Wadd greet you, for we are not permitted*
*the play of women, and religion has departed.*

As for Suwāʿ, it belonged to Hudhayl on the seacoast.

As for Yaghūth, it belonged to Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jurf in Saba, according to Qatadah.

Al-Mahdawi said: it belonged to Murad, then to Ghatafan. As for Yaʿūq, it belonged to Hamdan, according to Qatadah, Ikrimah, and ʿAtaʾ.

Al-Thaʿlabi said: it belonged to Kahlan ibn Saba, then they inherited it until it came to Hamdan. Malik ibn Namat al-Hamdani said of it:

*God makes feathers grow in this world and makes it fall away,*
*but Yaʿūq does not make it fall away, nor does he make feathers grow.*

As for Nasr, it belonged to Dhu al-Kalaʿ of Himyar, according to Qatadah and Muqatil.

The majority read *Waddan* with a fatha on the *waw*. Nafiʿ read it with a damma.

Al-Layth said: *Wudd* with a damma is an idol of Quraysh, and with a fatha it is an idol that belonged to the people of Noah. Amr ibn Wadd was named after it.

The majority read *wa-lā Yaghūtha wa-Yaʿūqa* without tanwin. If they are Arabic, the prohibition from declension is due to proper-noun status and the form of the verb. If they are foreign, it is due to foreignness and proper-noun status.

Al-Aʿmash read *wa-lā Yaghūthan wa-Yaʿūqan* with tanwin.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: that is an error.

The reason these idols are specifically mentioned, although they are included among the gods, is that they were the greatest and most important of their idols.

The pronoun for rational beings was applied to them because the disbelievers who worship them believe that they reason. ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in misguidance﴾ is coordinated with ﴿My Lord, they have disobeyed me﴾. The explicit noun was placed in place of the pronoun to record their wrongdoing against them.

Abu Hayyan said: it is coordinated with *qad aḍallū* ("they have led astray"). The meaning of ﴿except in misguidance﴾ is "except in punishment." Thus said Ibn Bahr, and he cited as evidence His saying: ﴿Indeed the criminals are in misguidance and madness﴾ [al-Qamar: 47]. It was also said: except in loss. It was also said: except in trial through wealth and children. It was also said: perdition. It was also said: misguidance in their scheme.

﴿Because of their sins they were drowned﴾. *Mā* is extra for emphasis, and the meaning is "because of their sins," that is, on account of them and because of them, they were drowned by the flood. ﴿Then they were made to enter a fire﴾ immediately after that, which is the fire of the Hereafter. It was also said: it is the punishment of the grave.

The majority read *khaṭīʾātihim* in the sound plural. Abu ʿAmr read *khaṭāyāhum* in the broken plural. Al-Jahdari, Amr ibn ʿUbayd, al-Aʿmash, Abu Hayawa, and Ashhab al-ʿUqayli read *khaṭīʾatihim* in the singular.

Al-Dahhak said: they were punished with fire in this world together with drowning, in one state: they were drowned on one side and burned on another.

The majority read *ughriqū* from *aghraqa*. Zayd ibn ʿAli read *ghurriqū* with doubling.

﴿Then they found for themselves no helpers besides God﴾, meaning they found no one to prevent them from God's punishment or to repel it from them.

﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as an inhabitant"﴾. This is coordinated with ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me"﴾. When Noah, peace be upon him, despaired of their faith and their turning away from disbelief, he invoked destruction against them.

Qatadah said: he invoked against them after it had been revealed to him: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]. God answered his supplication and drowned them.

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Muqatil, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, Ibn Zayd, and ʿAtiyyah said: he said this when God had brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women, and had made the wombs of women and the loins of men barren seventy years before the punishment. It was also said: forty years.

Qatadah said: there was no child among them at the time of the punishment.

Al-Hasan and Abu al-ʿAliyah said: if God had destroyed their children together with them, it would have been a punishment from God upon them and justice concerning them. But God destroyed their offspring and children without punishment, then destroyed them with punishment.

The *waw* was changed to a *yāʾ* and one of the two was assimilated into the other, like *al-qayyām*, whose origin is *qaywām*. Al-Qutaybi said: its origin is from *al-dār* ("the house"), meaning one who dwells in the house. It is said: *mā bi-l-dār dayyār*, meaning, "there is no one in the house." ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾, meaning if You leave them upon the earth, they will lead Your servants astray from the path of truth. ﴿And they will not beget except a wicked disbeliever﴾, meaning except one who will be wicked by abandoning Your obedience, a disbeliever of Your blessing, that is, one who greatly denies it. The meaning is: except one who will be wicked and will disbelieve.

Then, when he had invoked against the disbelievers, he followed it with supplication for himself, his parents, and the believers, saying: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾. They were both believers. His father was Lamak ibn Mutushalakh, as mentioned earlier, and his mother was Samhaʾ bint Anush. It was also said that he meant Adam and Eve.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: by "his parents" he meant his father and his grandfather.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr read *wa-li-wālidī* with a kasra on the *dāl*, in the singular.

In *al-Sihah* it is said: *al-Wadd* with a fatha is a peg in the dialect of the people of Najd, as though they had made the *tāʾ* quiescent and assimilated it into the *dāl*.

The majority read *wa-lā Yaghūtha wa-Yaʿūqa* without tanwin. If they are Arabic, the prohibition from declension is due to proper-noun status and the form of the verb. If they are foreign, it is due to foreignness and proper-noun status.

Al-Aʿmash read *wa-lā Yaghūthan wa-Yaʿūqan* with tanwin.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: that is an error.

The reason these idols are specifically mentioned, although they are included among the gods, is that they were the greatest and most important of their idols.

﴿And they have led many astray﴾, meaning their great ones and leaders led many people astray. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the idols, meaning that many people were led astray through them, like Abraham's saying: ﴿My Lord, they have led many people astray﴾ [Ibrahim: 36]. The pronoun for rational beings was applied to them because the disbelievers who worship them believe that they reason. ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in misguidance﴾ is coordinated with ﴿My Lord, they have disobeyed me﴾. The explicit noun was placed in place of the pronoun to record their wrongdoing against them.

Abu Hayyan said: it is coordinated with *qad aḍallū* ("they have led astray"). The meaning of ﴿except in misguidance﴾ is "except in punishment." Thus said Ibn Bahr, and he cited as evidence His saying: ﴿Indeed the criminals are in misguidance and madness﴾ [al-Qamar: 47]. It was also said: except in loss. It was also said: except in trial through wealth and children. It was also said: perdition. It was also said: misguidance in their scheme.

﴿Because of their sins they were drowned﴾. *Mā* is extra for emphasis, and the meaning is "because of their sins," that is, on account of them and because of them, they were drowned by the flood. ﴿Then they were made to enter a fire﴾ immediately after that, which is the fire of the Hereafter. It was also said: it is the punishment of the grave.

The majority read *khaṭīʾātihim* in the sound plural. Abu ʿAmr read *khaṭāyāhum* in the broken plural. Al-Jahdari, Amr ibn ʿUbayd, al-Aʿmash, Abu Hayawa, and Ashhab al-ʿUqayli read *khaṭīʾatihim* in the singular.

Al-Dahhak said: they were punished with fire in this world together with drowning, in one state: they were drowned on one side and burned on another.

The majority read *ughriqū* from *aghraqa*. Zayd ibn ʿAli read *ghurriqū* with doubling.

﴿Then they found for themselves no helpers besides God﴾, meaning they found no one to prevent them from God's punishment or to repel it from them.

﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as an inhabitant"﴾. This is coordinated with ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me"﴾. When Noah, peace be upon him, despaired of their faith and their turning away from disbelief, he invoked destruction against them.

Qatadah said: he invoked against them after it had been revealed to him: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]. God answered his supplication and drowned them.

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Muqatil, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, Ibn Zayd, and ʿAtiyyah said: he said this when God had brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women, and had made the wombs of women and the loins of men barren seventy years before the punishment. It was also said: forty years.

Qatadah said: there was no child among them at the time of the punishment.

Al-Hasan and Abu al-ʿAliyah said: if God had destroyed their children together with them, it would have been a punishment from God upon them and justice concerning them. But God destroyed their offspring and children without punishment, then destroyed them with punishment.

The meaning of *dayyāran* is one who inhabits dwellings. Its origin is *daywār*, on the pattern *fayʿāl*, from *dāra yadūru*. The *waw* was changed to a *yāʾ* and one of the two was assimilated into the other, like *al-qayyām*, whose origin is *qaywām*. Al-Qutaybi said: its origin is from *al-dār* ("the house"), meaning one who dwells in the house. It is said: *mā bi-l-dār dayyār*, meaning, "there is no one in the house." It was also said: *al-dayyār* is the owner of dwellings. The meaning is: do not spare anyone of them, but destroy him.

﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾, meaning if You leave them upon the earth, they will lead Your servants astray from the path of truth. ﴿And they will not beget except a wicked disbeliever﴾, meaning except one who will be wicked by abandoning Your obedience, a disbeliever of Your blessing, that is, one who greatly denies it. The meaning is: except one who will be wicked and will disbelieve.

Then, when he had invoked against the disbelievers, he followed it with supplication for himself, his parents, and the believers, saying: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾. They were both believers. His father was Lamak ibn Mutushalakh, as mentioned earlier, and his mother was Samhaʾ bint Anush. It was also said that he meant Adam and Eve.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: by "his parents" he meant his father and his grandfather.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr read *wa-li-wālidī* with a kasra on the *dāl*, in the singular.

﴿And for whoever enters my house﴾. Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: it means his mosque. It was also said: his dwelling in which he lived. It was also said: his ship. It was also said: whoever enters his religion. The accusative of *muʾminan* is circumstantial, meaning: whoever enters my house being characterized by the attribute of faith. Thus whoever enters it without being characterized by this attribute is excluded, such as his wife and his son, who said: ﴿I will take refuge in a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾ [Hud: 43]. Then he generalized the supplication, saying: ﴿and for the believing men and believing women﴾, meaning: forgive every person characterized by faith, male and female.

Then he returned to invoking against the disbelievers, saying: ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction﴾, meaning do not increase those characterized by wrongdoing except in ruin, loss, and destruction. His supplication included every wrongdoer until the Day of Resurrection, just as it included every believing man and believing woman until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Nor Wadd, nor Suwāʿ, nor Yaghūth, nor Yaʿūq, nor Nasr﴾, that he said: these idols were worshipped in the time of Noah.

Al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh related from him that he said: the idols that were worshipped among the people of Noah passed into the Arabs.

As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb at Dawmat al-Jandal. As for Suwāʿ, it belonged to Hudhayl. As for Yaghūth, it belonged to Murad, then to the Banu Ghutayf. As for Yaʿūq, it belonged to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Himyar, to the family of Dhu al-Kalaʿ. These were names of righteous men from the people of Noah. When they died, Satan revealed to their people: "Set up at their assembly place, where they used to sit, memorials (*anṣāb*), and name them after their names." They did so. It was not worshipped until those people had died, and knowledge was abrogated, and then it was worshipped.

**Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, on Surah 71, verses 21–28**

His saying: ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me"﴾, meaning they persisted in their disobedience and did not respond to my call. He complained of them to God, Mighty and Majestic, and informed Him that they had disobeyed him and had not followed him, though He knows this best. ﴿And they followed one whose wealth and children increased him only in loss﴾, meaning the lowly followed their leaders and the wealthy among them, whose abundance of wealth and children increased them only in misguidance in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

The people of Medina, the people of Syria, and ʿAsim, along with Waladuhu, read *wa-waladuhu* with a fatha on the *waw* and the *lam*.

The rest read it with a sukun on the *lam*. This is a dialectal form for "child" (*walad*). It may also be a plural. Its verification has already been discussed. The meaning of *wa-ittaba'u* ("and they followed") is that they persisted in following, not that they initiated the following.

﴿And they schemed a great scheme﴾, meaning a great, mighty scheme. It is said *kabīr*, *kubār*, and *kubbār*, like *ʿajīb*, *ʿujāb*, and *ʿujjāb*, and *jamīl*, *jumāl*, and *jummāl*.

Al-Mubarrad said: *kubbāran* with the doubled consonant is intensive, like *qurrāʾ* (very much reciting) for one who recites much. Ibn al-Sikkit recited:

*A fair one who hunts hearts and takes captive,*
*by beauty, the heart of the Muslim reciters.*

The majority read *kubbāran* with the doubled consonant. Ibn Muhaysin, Humayd, and Mujahid read it without doubling.

Abu Bakr said: it is the plural of *kabīr*, as though he made *makr* ("scheme") stand in place of *dhunūb* or *afāʿīl*, which is why he described it with the plural.

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: it is a Yemeni dialect form.

They differed about what this scheme was. It was said: it was their inciting their lowly ones to kill Noah. It was said: it was their deceiving people by means of the wealth and children they had been given, to the point that the weak said, "If they were not upon the truth, they would not have been given these blessings." (p-1536)

Al-Kalbi said: it was what they attributed to God of companions and offspring.

Muqatil said: it was the saying of their great ones to their followers, "Do not leave your gods." It was also said: their scheme was their disbelief.

﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods"﴾, meaning do not abandon the worship of your gods, which are the idols and images that they had. Later the Arabs worshipped them after them. This is the view of the majority. ﴿Nor Wadd, nor Suwāʿ, nor Yaghūth, nor Yaʿūq, nor Nasr﴾, meaning: do not abandon the worship of these.

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: these were names of righteous people who lived between Adam and Noah. After them, a generation arose that imitated them in worship. Iblis said to them, "If you made their images, it would be more invigorating for you and more conducive to worship." They did so. Then another generation arose after them, and Iblis said to them, "Those who came before you worshipped them, so worship them." The beginning of idol worship was from that time, and these images were named after these names because they had made them in the form of those people.

ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr and others said: these were names of Adam's children, and Wadd was the eldest of them.

Al-Mawardi said: as for Wadd, he was the first idol worshipped. He was named Wadd because of their love (*wudd*) for him. He was after the people of Noah, belonging to the tribe of Kalb at Dawmat al-Jandal, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtaʾ, and Muqatil. Their poet said of him:

*May Wadd greet you, for we are not permitted*
*the play of women, and religion has departed.*

As for Suwāʿ, it belonged to Hudhayl on the seacoast.

As for Yaghūth, it belonged to Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jurf in Saba, according to Qatadah.

Al-Mahdawi said: it belonged to Murad, then to Ghatafan. As for Yaʿūq, it belonged to Hamdan, according to Qatadah, Ikrimah, and ʿAtaʾ.

Al-Thaʿlabi said: it belonged to Kahlan ibn Saba, then they inherited it until it came to Hamdan. Malik ibn Namat al-Hamdani said of it:

*God makes feathers grow in this world and makes it fall away,*
*but Yaʿūq does not make it fall away, nor does he make feathers grow.*

As for Nasr, it belonged to Dhu al-Kalaʿ of Himyar, according to Qatadah and Muqatil.
